Grounded code keeps the terminal's colours inside a quote (rich-unfiled-791c.rm6p)

Review of #440 (high): at 16 colours `groundedStyle` dropped code's colours to
unset, so the quote's new magenta showed through and code in a quote drew bold
magenta, against docs/markdown.md's "in the terminal's own colours". It now
names `default on default`, which is what its header already promised; Rich's
code likewise keeps its own colours over a quote's.

The quote's style name is one constant again for the bar, its body and its
images' alt text; the docs say the style lies under the quote's blocks rather
than colouring all of them; console.test's theme table gains the name.

Markdown draws a quote's bar as ▌ in markdown.block_quote, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.rm6p)

Rich's BlockQuote draws its bar and the blocks it holds in the one
markdown.block_quote style (magenta). The port drew the bar ▎ in
markdown.hr and the body in a hardcoded dim italic; both now read the
one theme entry, so a theme restyles the whole quote.

Markdown draws a code block inside Syntax's margin, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.ct7i) (#439)

* Markdown draws a code block inside Syntax's margin, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.ct7i)

Rich's CodeBlock hands the code, rstripped, to Syntax(word_wrap=True,
padding=1). The block now draws through our Syntax the same way: word-wrapped
at width-2, tab stops of 4 (was 8), and a one-cell margin of the code's style
on every side. Trailing whitespace is Python's str.isspace set, not JS's \s.
Pinned against Rich 15 rows, including widths 1 and 2 where Rich draws only
the margin.

* Markdown pads a code block with Padding and strips it in one pass (rich-unfiled-791c.ct7i review)

The trailing-whitespace regex was quadratic in an interior run; pyRstrip
scans from the end over the one PY_WHITESPACE set. The hand-built margin
is Padding, so at widths under three the code keeps a column before the
padding does, as every Padding does. The width is parsed once at the top
of Markdown.render.
